system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.
region_name: Northern Hemisphere high-latitude and high-altitude regions

data_description.dataset_name: MOD09CMG.061 Terra Surface Reflectance Daily L3 Global 0.05 Deg CMG

spatial_coverage.region_name: Northern Hemisphere high-latitude and high-altitude regions
spatial_coverage.coverage: Global land coverage on the 0.05 degree Climate Modeling Grid, including boreal forest, tundra, alpine meadow and high-altitude sparse vegetation of the Northern Hemisphere.

analytical_capabilities: Computing vegetation, water or burn indices from atmospherically corrected reflectance
Building sub-monthly composites and deriving seasonal transition dates by curve fitting
Mapping spatial gradients in surface state across latitude and elevation belts
Detecting long-term trends, anomalies and abrupt changes in reflectance-derived indices
Combining reflectance with thermal brightness temperature for joint surface-state analysis

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Surface reflectance as a dimensionless fraction (bands 1-7); brightness temperature in kelvin (thermal bands 20, 21, 31, 32)
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Reflectance lives in `Coarse_Resolution_Surface_Reflectance_Band_1` through `_Band_7`; valid range is about -0.01 to 1.6. Scale factors and offsets are already applied in Earth Engine, so use values as-is. Red is band 1 and near-infrared is band 2, so NDVI is (Band_2 - Band_1) / (Band_2 + Band_1). Screen observations with `Coarse_Resolution_QA` (bits 0-1 carry overall quality, bits 2-29 give per-band quality), `Coarse_Resolution_State_QA` (cloud state, cloud shadow, land/water, aerosol, snow) and `Coarse_Resolution_Internal_CM` (internal cloud, snow, fire, sun glint, dust flags). Daily acquisition means heavy cloud and snow gaps at high latitudes, so build composites and interpolate explicitly before fitting seasonal curves. `number_of_500m_pixels_averaged_b3` and `n_pixels_averaged` report how many finer pixels contributed, flagging cells built from sparse observations. `Coarse_Resolution_Granule_Time` encodes acquisition time as HHMM, and `Coarse_Resolution_Solar_Zenith_Angle` matters at high latitudes where low sun angles bias retrievals.

data_description.data_source: NASA LP DAAC at the USGS EROS Center, derived from Terra MODIS
